messages.text: Gurney called up to World Series Finals after withdrawals due to visa issues

metadata.summary: Daryl Gurney has been called up to play at the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam after visa issues led to the withdrawal of Philippines players Lourence Ilagan and Alexis Toylo from the September 17-20 event.
metadata.content: World Series of Darts Finals: 2026 schedule and results with Luke Littler, Luke Humphries, Michael van Gerwen, Gian van Veen in action | Darts News | Sky Sports Skip to content World Series of Darts Finals: 2026 schedule and results with Luke Littler, Luke Humphries, Michael van Gerwen, Gian van Veen in action A top prize of £100,000 will be up for grabs at the 2026 World Series of Darts Finals featuring a blockbuster 32-player field, with tournament to commence on September 17 in Amsterdam Wednesday 9 September 2026 19:43, UK Image: Daryl Gurney will play reigning champion Michael van Gerwen in round one Daryl Gurney has been called up to play at the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam after visa issues led to the withdrawal of Philippines players Lourence Ilagan and Alexis Toylo from the September 17-20 event. Northern Ireland's Gurney and the Netherlands' Maik Kuivenhoven were the highest-ranked players on the reserve list and have replaced Ilagan and Toylo respectively after the pair did not receive a decision on their Schengen visa applications before having to travel to China this week for the final two events of the PDC Asian Tour season. Gurney will face reigning tournament champion and home favourite Michael van Gerwen in the first round at AFAS Live on Thursday September 17, while Kuivenhoven plays Jonny Clayton the following day. messages.text: Merson: Arsenal didn't make X-factor signing to win Champions League

metadata.summary: Arsenal's record last year was amazing in the Champions League and they're going to be there or thereabouts again – but I don't think they bought that X factor signing to take them to that next level.
metadata.content: Arsenal didn't make X factor signing like Vinicius Junior or Julian Alvarez to win Champions League, says Paul Merson | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Analysis Arsenal didn't make X factor signing like Vinicius Junior or Julian Alvarez to win Champions League, says Paul Merson Paul Merson gives his verdict on Arsenal's Champions League hopes in his latest column; Sky Sports pundit believes Gunners needed more than Kai Havertz up front; Follow Napoli vs Arsenal on the Sky Sports app with our dedicated match commentary from 6.30pm on Wednesday Paul Merson Football Expert & Columnist @PaulMerse Wednesday 9 September 2026 15:58, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Paul Merson has his say on whether Arsenal will have a chance at claiming Champions League glory. Arsenal's record last year was amazing in the Champions League and they're going to be there or thereabouts again – but I don't think they bought that X factor signing to take them to that next level. They have enough to win the Premier League with their squad. I just think the forward line against the big boys, they're missing that little ingredient. If they'd had a Vinicius Junior or a Julian Alvarez, that would have given them the edge to go on and win the Champions League. I think they might just fall short. messages.text: Chandhok: Not driving for Ferrari has taken pressure off Antonelli

metadata.summary: Sky Sports F1's Karun Chandhok believes Kimi Antonelli driving for Mercedes, rather than Ferrari, has taken some pressure off the Italian.
metadata.content: Kimi Antonelli driving for Mercedes rather than Ferrari has taken pressure off Italian says Karun Chandhok | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Opinion Kimi Antonelli driving for Mercedes rather than Ferrari has taken pressure off Italian says Karun Chandhok On the latest episode of Sky Sports F1's The F1 Show, Simon Lazenby, Karun Chandhok and David Croft discuss Kimi Antonelli's stunning win at Monza; watch every session of the Spanish Grand Prix at a new track in Madrid from this Friday, live on Sky Sports F1 Karun Chandhok F1 Expert Wednesday 9 September 2026 15:15, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch how Kimi Antonelli converted 19th to first to take a sensational victory at the Italian Grand Prix Sky Sports F1's Karun Chandhok believes Kimi Antonelli driving for Mercedes, rather than Ferrari, has taken some pressure off the Italian. Antonelli joined the Mercedes junior programme as an 11-year-old after some remarkable results in karting and quickly rose up the motorsport ranks to Formula 1 and replaced Lewis Hamilton at the Silver Arrows only last year. He currently leads the Drivers' Championship by 66 points from team-mate George Russell ahead of this weekend's Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid and is on course to become the youngest world champion in F1 history at 20 years old.
